h.strategy: Most obvious hypotheses follow a local story: an option matters more when its substitute is missing. These are usually rated likely and often fail. Instead, base hypotheses on robust statistical regularities. (1) Headroom: helpful edits help less in parents that are already strong, for example parents that already contain the strongest option elsewhere. (2) Harmful edits hurt more in strong parents and look harmless in weak parents, because of floor effects. (3) Saturation: adding a second copy of a strong option gives smaller gains than adding the first. (4) Removing an option costs less when the parent has several similar options. Choose conditions that many parents satisfy, so the effect is detectable. Cover several edited fields and both directions. In each 'why', state the obvious prediction and the reason the opposite should hold.

hyps.why: Removing an edge costs less when a similar strong edge into node 3 remains to compensate.
With a parallel 3x3 conv feeding node 3, dropping edge 5 is largely compensated, so the loss is smaller.
Cutting 0->1 hurts less when node 2 still receives a strong conv directly from the input, since a similar alternative path exists.
Obvious: conv beats anything; but the skip on the direct input-to-output edge is already a strong, cheap path, so replacing it gains less than replacing a weak op.
A second skip into the output adds little over an existing direct skip, so its benefit is smaller than in parents without one.
Obvious: skips help gradient flow; but a second skip into node 3 is redundant with the first, so the gain saturates.
Parents already containing a strong 3x3 conv near the output sit closer to the ceiling, so the 1x1 gain is smaller.
When a strong 3x3 conv already feeds node 3, adding a 1x1 on the direct edge is largely redundant.
A 1x1 conv is a modest upgrade and gains less when a stronger 3x3 conv already feeds node 3 through the parallel edge.
Obvious: a conv early on feeds the strong downstream edge and compounds; opposite holds because a parent that already contains a 3x3 conv has less headroom for another.
